item.title: The Cost of a Closure in C
item.description:
📝 Closures in this instance are programming language constructs that includes data alongside instructions that are not directly related to their input (arguments) and their results (return values). , the set of closures that do not include this extra, spicy data that comes from places outside of arguments and returns). It becomes more pronounced when you want to do things with function and data that are a bit more complex, such as Donald Knuth’s “Man-or-Boy” test code.
🔗 Read more: https://thephd.dev/the-cost-of-a-closure-in-c-c2y
